prompt.context_jp: 夕方のマーケティング課には、いつもと違う張り詰めた空気が漂っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 夕方のマーケティング課___、いつもと違う張り詰めた空気が漂っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that marks the location as a topic/setting.

feedback.correct_en: には combines location に with topic は — 'as for in the marketing department...' It establishes the setting as the topic being described.
feedback.incorrect_en: The other combinations are ungrammatical particle stacks and don't fit a location-as-topic frame.

contrast_examples.en: In the classroom, there are students.

prompt.context_jp: 事情は課内に響き渡っていたはずだが、彼女の表情には波ひとつ立っていない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 事情は課内に響き渡っていたはずだが、彼女の表情___波ひとつ立っていない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that creates the contrast between the department's reaction and her face.

feedback.correct_en: には marks '彼女の表情' as the location of the (non-)event, with は adding contrast — unlike the department as a whole, on her face nothing stirred.
feedback.incorrect_en: では would suggest a means or an abstract domain; the natural reading here is a physical location (on her face).

contrast_examples.jp: 顔には何も出ていない。

prompt.context_jp: 会社の綱領に何と書いてあろうと、いま頼めるのは彼女しかいなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: いま頼める___彼女しかいなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that marks the exhaustive 'only she' identification.

feedback.correct_en: のは sets up a topic-focus structure: 'as for the one he could ask now, it was only her.' The identifying predicate (彼女しかいなかった) requires は, not が.
feedback.incorrect_en: のが would make 'the one he could ask' a new subject needing another predicate; it doesn't close the cleft naturally here.

contrast_examples.en: The one who came was her.

prompt.context_jp: 定時のチャイムが天井から降ってきた瞬間、春子はまるでその音を待っていたかのように立ち上がった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 定時のチャイム___天井から降ってきた瞬間、春子はまるでその音を待っていたかのように立ち上がった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that marks the chime as new information in a time clause.

feedback.correct_en: Inside a 瞬間 (moment) subordinate clause, the subject takes が as a new event being described. は would wrongly turn it into a main topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would strand the clause and conflict with the sentence's main topic 春子.

contrast_examples.jp: 雨が降った瞬間、走り出した。
contrast_examples.en: The moment it rained, I ran.

prompt.context_jp: 東海林: 「この人は 残業も休日出勤も 絶対しないから」
prompt.prompt_jp: この人___残業も休日出勤も絶対しないから。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that marks 'этот person' as the contrastive topic.

feedback.correct_en: は singles out Haruko as a topic contrasted with everyone else — 'this one, unlike us, never does overtime.' That contrastive framing is central to Shoji's point.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark her as new/exhaustive subject, but the sentence is characterizing her ongoing policy, which needs topic は.

contrast_examples.en: He's the one who won't drink.

prompt.context_jp: 東海林の額には汗が浮き、里中はネクタイを緩めることさえ忘れている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 東海林の額には汗___浮き、里中はネクタイを緩めることさえ忘れている。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 'sweat beading up' as a newly observed detail.

feedback.correct_en: 汗が浮き describes a newly observed physical event — perceptual が for new information. The topic frame (額には) is already set.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would clash with the already-marked topic 額には and would wrongly promote 汗 to topic status.

contrast_examples.en: Tears well up in his eyes.

prompt.context_jp: 里中: 「東海林さんは こんなピンチ 何度も乗り越えてきたんだから」
prompt.prompt_jp: 東海林さん___こんなピンチ、何度も乗り越えてきたんだから。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that frames Shoji as the topic of a general characterization.

feedback.correct_en: は presents Shoji as the topic the speaker is characterizing — his track record of overcoming crises. This is encouragement framed as a known fact about him.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it sound like identifying who overcame crises (as if answering a who-question), not fitting this reassurance.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼は何度も成功している。

contrast_examples.en: He was the one who succeeded.

prompt.context_jp: 返事はまだ、返らない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 返事___まだ、返らない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that frames 'the reply' as the known topic.

feedback.correct_en: The reply is already discourse-given (we were waiting for it). は marks it as topic, often with an implied contrast ('as for a reply — not yet').
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce 返事 as new information, but it has already been set up by context as the thing being awaited.

prompt.context_jp: ママ: 「私は ほら イケメンじゃないとダメなのよね」
prompt.prompt_jp: 私___ほら、イケメンじゃないとダメなのよね。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that contrasts 'me' with 'you'.

feedback.correct_en: Mom is contrasting her preferences with her daughter's. 私は sets up contrastive topic — 'as for me, I need a good-looking guy.'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would exhaustively identify 'I' as the one needing a hot guy, which misses the contrastive 'as opposed to you' nuance.

prompt.context_jp: 春子: 「あいつはね 仕事はできるんだけど… 派遣差別者」
prompt.prompt_jp: あいつはね、仕事___できるんだけど…派遣差別者。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that creates the 'can do X but...' contrast.

feedback.correct_en: 仕事はできる uses contrastive は — 'work-wise he's capable, BUT...' This は flags a positive point being set against a negative one.
feedback.incorrect_en: 仕事ができる (with が) just states a fact neutrally; it doesn't set up the 'but' contrast that follows.

contrast_examples.jp: 顔はいいが性格が悪い。
contrast_examples.en: Looks are fine, but personality is bad.

prompt.context_jp: ツネさん: 「俺も年だし もう潮時だな…」
prompt.prompt_jp: 俺___年だし、もう潮時だな…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle presenting '俺' as topic in self-description.

feedback.correct_en: も adds 'also/too' — 'I too am getting old.' It frames the speaker as one more case among others, fitting Tsune's resignation.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would just identify 'I' as the subject of being old, losing the 'me too' softening nuance.

prompt.context_jp: 彼女の背は真っ直ぐで、緊張のような色は一片も見えない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼女の背___真っ直ぐで、緊張のような色は一片も見えない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle presenting her back as topic in a description.

feedback.correct_en: は presents 彼女の背 as the topic being characterized ('as for her back, it's straight'). This is a descriptive statement about a known referent.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark it as new info ('her back is the thing that's straight'), which doesn't fit this descriptive narration.

prompt.context_jp: 春子: 「73キロ 本マグロ！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 見て！このマグロ___!
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle for calling attention to the tuna.

feedback.correct_en: 見る takes を for its object. 'このマグロ(を)見て' = 'look at this tuna!' The direct-object marker fits the imperative.
feedback.incorrect_en: が and は would reframe the tuna as a subject/topic, not as the thing being viewed.

prompt.context_jp: 春子: 「私は“Ｓ＆Ｆ”のために やったわけではなくて 友達のためにやったんです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 私___“Ｓ＆Ｆ”のためにやったわけではなくて、友達のためにやったんです。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle framing 'I' as the contrastive topic.

feedback.correct_en: は sets up Haruko's identity frame — 'as for me, it wasn't for S&F but for a friend.' The sentence contrasts two reasons, which requires topic は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would exhaustively identify 'I' as the actor, missing the 'not X but Y' contrast structure.

contrast_examples.jp: 私は会社のためじゃない。
contrast_examples.en: As for me, it's not for the company.
I'm the one who did it.

prompt.context_jp: 浅野匡子: 「会社は 恋愛をする所ではなく 仕事をする所です」
prompt.prompt_jp: 会社___恋愛をする所ではなく、仕事をする所です。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle framing 'the company' as topic for definition.

feedback.correct_en: This is a definitional, generic statement: 'As for the company, it's a place for work.' Generic definitions use は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would identify 'the company' exhaustively among alternatives, which doesn't fit a general principle statement.

prompt.context_jp: 里中: 「大前さんも 協力していただけますか？」 春子の返事:
prompt.prompt_jp: 「___であれば」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose Haruko's characteristic phrasing for conditional cooperation.

feedback.correct_en: 業務時間内 ('within business hours') is formal, contractual language — exactly Haruko's register as a strictly-by-contract temp worker.
feedback.incorrect_en: 仕事中 is too casual; 会社の中 refers to location, not time. Neither captures her legalistic framing.

contrast_examples.jp: 業務時間内に対応します。
contrast_examples.en: I'll handle it within business hours.

contrast_examples.jp: 仕事中は電話に出ない。
contrast_examples.en: I don't take calls while working.

prompt.context_jp: 春子: 「ビジネスと私情を ___させるのは やめてください」
prompt.prompt_jp: ビジネスと私情を___させるのは やめてください。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb for mixing up two separate domains.

feedback.correct_en: 混同する means 'to confuse/conflate two things.' 混同させる = 'to make X and Y be confused/mixed up.' This is exactly what Haruko accuses him of doing.
feedback.incorrect_en: 混合 is physical mixing (chemicals); 混乱 is 'confusion/chaos' as a state. Only 混同 fits conflating categories.

prompt.context_jp: 春子が里中を店から追い出す場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「お___ください」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose Haruko's polite 'please leave' phrasing.

feedback.correct_en: お引き取りください is a formal, cold dismissal — 'please withdraw/leave.' It's the polite-but-firm phrasing fitting Haruko's icy register.
feedback.incorrect_en: お帰りください exists but is softer; お出かけください is nonsensical here. 引き取る specifically conveys 'take yourself away.'

prompt.context_jp: デパートの客に向けて東海林が深く謝罪する場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「誠に___ございません 本日の解体ショーは 中止とさせていただきます」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the formal apology phrasing.

feedback.correct_en: 誠に申し訳ございません is the standard formal business apology — 'we are truly sorry.' It's the highest register of 謝罪.
feedback.incorrect_en: 仕方ございません means 'it can't be helped' (not an apology); 問題ございません means 'no problem' (opposite meaning).

prompt.context_jp: 里中: 「東海林さんは 辞表を___に入れてんだよ！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 辞表を___に入れてんだよ！
prompt.prompt_en: Choose where Shoji has stashed his resignation letter.

feedback.correct_en: ポケットに入れる = 'carrying it on him' — Shoji literally has his resignation in his pocket, ready to submit. Earlier narration confirmed 'white paper edge peeking from his chest pocket.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 引き出し (drawer) or カバン (bag) would weaken the urgency; the point is he's prepared to resign right now.

contrast_examples.jp: 辞表をポケットに入れる。
contrast_examples.en: To carry a resignation in one's pocket.

contrast_examples.jp: 書類を引き出しに入れる。
contrast_examples.en: To put papers in a drawer.

prompt.context_jp: 春子: 「毎日 ___の上を 渡っているようなもんですから」
prompt.prompt_jp: 毎日___の上を渡っているようなもんですから。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word that makes the metaphor 'walking on the edge of danger'.

feedback.correct_en: 刃の上を渡る ('walking on a blade') captures the knife-edge precarity of temp work — one slip and you're cut. It also echoes the tuna-filleting knife imagery.
feedback.incorrect_en: 糸の上 (on a thread) and 氷の上 (on ice) exist as metaphors but aren't the phrase used, and the blade specifically fits temp-work precarity.

contrast_examples.jp: 刃の上を渡るような仕事。
contrast_examples.en: Work like walking on a knife's edge.
Feeling like treading on thin ice.

prompt.context_jp: 春子のステージ口上: 「どうぞ 財布の紐を ___ 締めて ご覧あれ！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 財布の紐を___締めてご覧あれ！
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the modifier for 'loosening the purse strings' showman-style.

feedback.correct_en: 緩く締める is a playful oxymoron ('tie it loosely') — Haruko's showman trick inviting the audience to spend freely. Perfect for the pitch patter.
feedback.incorrect_en: 固く/強く締める ('tie tightly/firmly') would tell customers to keep their money — the opposite of what a salesperson wants.

prompt.context_jp: 森美雪: 「皆さんに合わせて___してたけど、2000円のランチ 食べる余裕なんて ないんです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 皆さんに合わせて___してたけど…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the expression for 'stretching beyond one's means to fit in'.

feedback.correct_en: 背伸びする literally means 'standing on tiptoe' and figuratively 'stretching/pretending beyond one's level' — exactly what Miyuki admits to doing to fit in with wealthier colleagues.
feedback.incorrect_en: 背負い is 'carrying on one's back'; 背中 is just 'back' (noun). Neither forms the idiom for overreaching socially.

contrast_examples.jp: 背伸びして高い服を買う。
contrast_examples.en: To stretch oneself to buy expensive clothes.
To carry a load on one's back.

prompt.context_jp: 春子が里中に、仕事と友情を分ける原則を伝える場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural for Haruko's cool, professional refusal?

choices.text: それを派遣の私に頼むのは筋が違うと思います。
それを派遣の私に頼むのは道が違うと思います。
それを派遣の私に頼むのは線が違うと思います。

feedback.correct_en: 筋が違う ('that's not right / out of line') is a set phrase for 'this isn't the proper channel/logic.' It's exactly Haruko's crisp, principled register.
feedback.incorrect_en: 道が違う and 線が違う are not idiomatic for this meaning. Only 筋 collocates with 違う to mean 'improper / against reason'.

contrast_examples.en: That's not right / out of line.

prompt.context_jp: 里中が落ち込む東海林を励ます。
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural for 'getting through a crisis'?

choices.text: こんなピンチ、何度も乗り越えてきたんだから。
こんなピンチ、何度も越え渡ってきたんだから。
こんなピンチ、何度も飛び越してきたんだから。

feedback.correct_en: ピンチを乗り越える is the standard collocation for 'overcoming a tight spot/crisis.' 乗り越える specifically fits adversity.
feedback.incorrect_en: 越え渡る isn't a standard verb; 飛び越す ('to jump over') suggests a physical obstacle, not a difficult situation.

prompt.context_jp: 東海林が春子に特別手当の話をする。
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural for 'you can name your price'?

choices.text: いくらでも払うそうですよ。
いくらでも支払うそうですよ。
どのくらいでも払うそうですよ。

feedback.correct_en: いくらでも払う is the natural colloquial phrasing — 'they'll pay any amount.' いくらでも is the standard quantifier here.
feedback.incorrect_en: 支払う is more formal/stiff for spoken reassurance; どのくらいでも isn't idiomatic as a free-choice quantifier for money.

prompt.context_jp: 春子が東海林の懇願を拒絶する場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural for Haruko's firm refusal?

choices.text: お断りしますといったら、お断りします。
お断りすると言ったので、お断りします。
お断りしますとなれば、お断りします。

feedback.correct_en: The 〜といったら〜 pattern (repeating the same word) is a strong emphatic — 'when I say no, I mean no.' Perfectly matches Haruko's iron resolve.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜と言ったので〜 gives a causal 'because I said'; 〜となれば is conditional. Neither captures the emphatic repetition for refusal.

contrast_examples.jp: ダメだと言ったらダメ。
contrast_examples.en: When I say no, it's no.

contrast_examples.jp: 行くと言ったので行きます。
contrast_examples.en: Since I said I'd go, I'll go.

prompt.context_jp: 春子: 派遣仲間同士が助け合うのは当然と語る場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural for 'filling each other's gaps'?

choices.text: そういう者同士が穴を埋め合うのは当然のことです。
そういう者同士が穴を塞ぎ合うのは当然のことです。
そういう者同士が穴を補い合うのは当然のことです。

feedback.correct_en: 穴を埋める is the standard idiom for 'filling a gap/vacancy' (especially a work absence). 埋め合う reciprocates it — 'cover each other's gaps.' This matches the chapter's phrasing.
feedback.incorrect_en: 塞ぎ合う ('block each other up') carries wrong nuance; 補い合う works for 'supplement each other' but doesn't collocate with 穴 as naturally.

contrast_examples.en: To fill a gap / cover an absence.
